notes.filename: Are You Your Friends- Friend- Poor Perception of Friendship Ties Limits the Ability to Promote Behavioral Change.md
notes.claims_checked: Research questions and core associations are supported. Table 1 reports 76 observations; reciprocal-friend and incoming ‘ego perceived friend’ coefficients are positive/significant, while outgoing ‘alter perceived friend’ is not significant. The note correctly says the association is not a causal transition rule.

bibliography.issues: All captured references and their order match the original snapshot. This checks preservation, not completeness or title-by-title reconciliation.

exact_fixes: Correct the dependent-variable description in the analysis/model text: the article defines it as average daily activity during P2 divided by average daily activity during P1, rather than a generic activity ‘change’ or difference (Methods, intervention analysis; Table 1).

Disambiguate the paper’s counterintuitive labels: ‘ego perceived friend’ means an incoming nomination (alter names ego); ‘alter perceived friend’ means an outgoing nomination (ego names alter). State which was significant accordingly (Results, Table 1).

Replace the opaque Treatment GroupA/GroupB ellipsis with the actual control, Peer See, and Peer Reward arms, and note that the reported analysis pools the two peer-pressure conditions and omits control (Results, intervention analysis).

For the tie-type prediction component, name the reported classifier families and evaluation outcome rather than leaving the defining work entirely in predict_tie_type(...); the paper reports logistic regression and Random Forest results with ROC AUC (Results, Predicting Directionality).
notes.metadata: DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0151588 and publication date 2016-03-22 match the primary article.
corrections_applied: Rewrote intervention outcome as mean daily activity in P2 divided by mean daily activity in P1.
Defined authors’ direction labels: ego-perceived friend is an incoming nomination (alter→ego); alter-perceived friend is outgoing (ego→alter), and stated which coefficients are significant.
Enumerated Control, Peer See, and Peer Reward and noted the peer-pressure arms are pooled with control omitted for that analysis.
Named the logistic-regression and Random Forest classification procedures and ROC AUC evaluation; specified common-friend embeddedness and degree-centrality difference.
